title: Rav Bavahu
author: Aharon Hyman

paragraphs: So it is cited in Yuchasin: “Rav Bavahu said to Rav Ashi, at the end of chapter 2 of Yevamot,” and Seder HaDorot wrote, “I have not found it.” Hyman points to Bava Kamma 117a, “Rabbi Abbahu raised an objection to Rav Ashi,” and Dikdukei Soferim reads Rabbavahu (this Rabbi Abbahu was one of the heads of the kallah of Rafram, as explained in his entry). Likewise in Yevamot 26a, the reading of the Or Zarua HaGadol is “Rabbi Abbahu said to Rav Ashi.” Hyman considers Yuchasin’s reading there too undoubtedly Rabbavahu. In Chullin 49a, “Rabbi Shmuel son of Rabbi Abbahu said” — Dikdukei Soferim reads “son of Rabbavahu.” See his entry.

notes.text: Undoubtedly preserves Hyman’s force while keeping the Rabbavahu/Abbahu/Bavahu readings and proposed Yuchasin reading distinct. His head-of-kallah identification remains attributed rather than an independent identity merge.

Davidson Bava Kamma 117a directly reads Rabbi Abbahu raising an objection to Rav Ashi. Rabbavahu/Bavahu, the Or Zarua and Dikdukei Soferim readings, Rafram’s kallah identification and Hyman’s undoubtedly about Yuchasin remain distinguished, not silently merged.
